remaining_limit: S15: queued automation re-checked inside the applying write. S16: CaseApplyRecheck binds a check for the duration of an apply; every case-file write and every map link write runs it inside its own savepoint before its body. AI configured execution re-checks each effect's input versions (still in the case, still current) and the policy version it ran under; accepting a proposal re-checks its inputs; a carried job row re-checks that its result is still the current, intact (same digest, not superseded) revision of that job and that every reference that resolved when read still resolves. A refusal (CaseApplyRecheck.Refused) leaves nothing; compensating cancellations run unchecked. Tested by binding the checks over real writes; the AI execute path itself is covered by the S10 suites (unchanged behaviour when inputs are current), not by an in-flight change during a scripted run. A multi-write effect (create action, then its contract) can be refused at its second write, leaving the first (the task is then cancelled, as before).

requirement: RAR (RAR4/RAR5) and 7z through the system libarchive that ships with macOS (BSD licence, its own decoder — no proprietary code, no new package), and real readers for legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt (Word piece table, Excel BIFF8 cells, PowerPoint text atoms) over the existing OLE2 reader.
remaining_limit: T3: RAR4 now read through the system libarchive on a BSD-2-Clause Homebrew fixture (member listed, bytes exact). Not covered: RAR5, solid, multi-volume and passworded RAR samples. T2 (earlier): 7z read through the system libarchive on the two 7z fixtures; still no RAR sample. SystemArchiveReader dlopens /usr/lib/libarchive.2.dylib and streams RAR4/RAR5/7z members into the container flow (entry/byte caps, per-member cap, archive-wide ratio cap, root budget, disk reserve, unsafe paths, encrypted members recorded, nested recursion with cycle/depth limits); legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt use the structural readers first. Round 2 (R2-D 54745db9): .rar/.7z attachable; multi-volume archives read as one stream (archive_read_open_filenames) with the later volumes found beside the original (name.part1.rar → part2…, name.rar → .r00…, name.7z.001 → .002…; root archive only); passworded RAR/7z are classified 'needs a password' and the password-unlock flow opens them (archive_read_add_passphrase), adding each member as a readable copy linked to the archive (up to 10,000 members, 2 GB each, 16 GB in all). Limits: the libarchive calls were checked only by a python ctypes probe (no RAR sample run); later volumes are also imported as their own files (they fail to open alone and are recorded so); an encrypted multi-volume archive is unlocked from its first volume only; unlocked members are added as separate copies (not re-expanded as one container, so nested archives inside them expand as their own containers).

requirement: Torrent idea (owner 2026-11-23) — Choking: favour the fastest peers: Reading concurrency is set per disk, by measured throughput (SSD wide; USB, network or optical narrow).
remaining_limit: Speed torrent test phase 2026-11-23 (docs/evidence/speed-2026-11-23/TORRENT-TEST.md): Files are grouped by disk and dealt round-robin with the faster disk first. Each kind of disk starts at its own width and cap. One lane widens on rising bytes/s and narrows when bytes/s falls by a quarter, without touching another lane. A full lane makes a read wait. A nested read of the same disk reuses the held slot, with no deadlock past the width. In the bench, the internal-disk lane ended at width 10 (its cap) after the import.
